title: 2100 Bioanalyzer Operation for PCR, GTP and IVT Products
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfzjjp4n
materials: Electrode cleaner chips (included in all LabChip kits)
Rainin Pipetteman (p2, p10, p200, p1000, p20 repeater).
Dye contains DMSO, avoid contact with skin.
Wait 10 seconds, and open the lid.
Wait exactly 30 seconds, and release the clip.
Do not touch the bioanalyzer during an assay.
Take out two Nano Reagents Part II boxes from the MB5 -20°C freezer, thaw at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Wait 1 minute, and open the lid.

Denature for 5 minutes at 70°C in thermocycler with no heated lid. After denaturing, place on ice for a full 5 minutes, then spin down. During BA chip loading, the plate can remain on ice or on the bench-top cooler.

steps.title: Prepare DNA gel‑dye mix
steps.instruction: Allow DNA dye concentrate (blue vial) and DNA gel matrix (red vial) to equilibrate to room temperature for 30 min; vortex the dye concentrate, add 25 µl to the gel matrix tube, vortex again, spin down, and transfer the mixture to a DNA 7500 spin filter; centrifuge at 4000 g for 10 min, protect from light, store at 4 °C in the “DNA BA” box and use within 4 weeks.

steps.title: Obtain tracking sheet
steps.instruction: Retrieve the tracking sheet that lists the PCR or GTP samples to be run and record the run name (e.g., BA_YYMMDD_NN_PCR).

steps.title: Thaw PCR/GTP plate
steps.instruction: Thaw the PCR or GTP plate at room temperature for 3 min, spin down, replace the plate seal with a 96‑well rubber mat, and keep the plate sealed until loading.

steps.title: Clean Bioanalyzer electrodes (DNA assay)
steps.instruction: Pipette 350 µl of nuclease‑free dH₂O into a labeled electrode‑cleaner chip, ensuring the liquid reaches all well corners; place the chip in the Bioanalyzer, close the lid and verify software acknowledgment; remove the chip and wait 10 s for the water to evaporate; close the Bioanalyzer lid. Use a new electrode‑cleaner chip for each LabChip kit and never fill more than 350 µl.

steps.title: Prime DNA 7500 chip
steps.instruction: Set the chip priming station base plate to position “C” and the plunger to the topmost position; label a new DNA 7500 chip with sample information and run number; add 9.0 µl of the filtered gel‑dye mix to the well marked “G”; place the chip in the priming station, close it and press the plunger until it clips; wait 5 s, then slowly pull the plunger up to the 1 mL position; open the station and verify that capillaries are no longer visible (repeat priming if they are).

steps.title: Load DNA chip with marker and samples
steps.instruction: Add 9.0 µl gel‑dye mix to each of the remaining two “G” wells; add 5 µl DNA 7500 marker (green vial) to the ladder well and to each of the 12 sample wells; add 1.0 µl DNA 7500 ladder (yellow vial) to the ladder picture well; add 1.0 µl of each diluted PCR or GTP sample to its respective sample well, changing tips between samples; ensure each sample well contains exactly 5.0 µl total volume; insert pipette tips to the bottom of wells to avoid bubbles; protect all dye and mixtures from light.

steps.title: Vortex DNA chip
steps.instruction: Place the loaded DNA chip in an IKA vortex mixer and vortex at 2200 rpm for exactly 1 min.

steps.title: Run DNA chip on Bioanalyzer
steps.instruction: Within 5 min of loading, open the 2100 Expert program, place the chip inside the Bioanalyzer and close the lid; select “Instrument” → “Assay…”, choose “DNA 7500 Series II” (dsDNA); in the File Prefix field type “BA_YYMMDD_NN_PCR” (YY=year, MM=month, DD=day, NN=run number of the day); click “Start”; once the assay starts, click “Data” → “Chip Summary”; view gel pictures and electropherograms via the “Gel” and “Electropherogram” tabs; the run takes ~30 min.

steps.title: Post‑run cleanup (DNA)
steps.instruction: Remove the LabChip from the Bioanalyzer and dispose of it; clean the electrodes as described in step 4; empty the electrode‑cleaner chip at the end of the day.

steps.title: Prepare RNA gel‑dye mix (IVT assay)
steps.instruction: Allow RNA gel matrix (red vial) to equilibrate to room temperature for 30 min; pipette 550 µl of RNA 6000 Nano gel mix (red vial) into an RNA 6000 spin filter and centrifuge at 4000 g for 10 min; aliquot 65 µl of filtered gel into RNase‑free 0.5 ml tubes, label with “gel” and date, store at 4 °C in the “RNA BA” box and use within 4 weeks; vortex the RNA 6000 Nano dye concentrate (blue vial) for 10 s, spin down, add 1.0 µl dye concentrate to each 65 µl gel aliquot, vortex, spin at 13 000 rpm for 10 min at room temperature, protect from light, and label the tube with the date (this mix must be made fresh on the day of the run).

steps.title: Prepare RNA ladder
steps.instruction: Vortex and transfer 35 µl of each RNA 6000 ladder into two 0.65 ml tubes; heat‑denature at 70 °C for 2 min, then place on a bench‑top cooler for 5 min; dispense 2.2 µl into each tube using a single‑channel P20 repeater; label tubes with “L, date”; store at –80 °C in the “RNA ladder aliquot” box (one aliquot suffices for two LabChips).

steps.title: Thaw IVT plate
steps.instruction: Thaw the IVT plate from –80 °C at room temperature for ~3 min, spin down, remove the plate seal and cover with a 96‑well rubber mat; initial and date the side of the plate to indicate it has been denatured (critical to keep product snapped in position).

steps.title: Clean Bioanalyzer electrodes (RNA assay)
steps.instruction: Pipette 350 µl of nuclease‑free dH₂O into a labeled electrode‑cleaner chip; place the chip in the Bioanalyzer, close the lid and verify software acknowledgment; remove the chip and wait 10 s for water to evaporate; close the Bioanalyzer lid. Use a new electrode‑cleaner chip each run and never exceed 350 µl.

steps.title: Prime RNA chip
steps.instruction: Set the chip priming station base plate to position “C” and the plunger to the topmost position; label a new RNA chip with sample information and run number; add 9.0 µl of the prepared RNA gel‑dye mix to the well marked “G”; place the chip in the priming station, close it and press the plunger until it clips; wait 5 s, then slowly pull the plunger up to the 1 mL position; open the station and verify capillaries are no longer visible (repeat priming if needed).

steps.title: Load RNA chip with marker and samples
steps.instruction: Add 9.0 µl gel‑dye mix to each of the two “G” wells; add 5.0 µl RNA 6000 marker (green vial) to the ladder well and each of the 12 sample wells; add 1.0 µl RNA 6000 ladder (yellow vial) to the ladder picture well; add 1.0 µl denatured IVT sample to each sample well, changing tips between samples; ensure each sample well contains exactly 5.0 µl total volume; insert pipette tips to the bottom of wells to avoid bubbles; protect all dye and mixtures from light.

steps.title: Vortex RNA chip
steps.instruction: Place the loaded RNA chip in an IKA vortex mixer and vortex at 2200 rpm for exactly 1 min.

steps.title: Run RNA chip on Bioanalyzer
steps.instruction: Within 5 min of loading, open the 2100 Expert program, place the chip inside the Bioanalyzer and close the lid; select “Instrument” → “Assay…”, choose “Eukaryote Total RNA Nano Series II”; in the File Prefix field type “BA_YYMMDD_NN_IVT” (YY=year, MM=month, DD=day, NN=run number of the day) and record the run name on the “PCR to IVT” coversheet; click “Start”; once the assay starts, click “Data” → “Chip Summary”; enter sample information for each of the 12 samples in the format “IVT_YYMMDD_PP_RCC” (YYMMDD=date of sample plate, PP=plate number, R=row, CC=column); view gel pictures and electropherograms via the “Gel” and “Electropherogram” tabs; the run takes ~30 min.

steps.title: Post‑run cleanup (RNA)
steps.instruction: Remove the LabChip from the Bioanalyzer and dispose of it; clean the electrodes as described in step 12; empty the electrode‑cleaner chips at the end of the day.

description: Click the “Chip Summary” tab and enter the sample information for each of the 12 samples in the format “PCR_YYMMDD_PP_RCC” (or “GTP_YYMMDD_PP_RCC”) where YYMMDD=date of the sample plate, PP=sample plate number, R=sample row from sample plate, and CC=sample column from sample plate.
